world.title: Car bomb kills father and child in Damascus suburb; authorities investigate
world.summary: A bomb planted in a car exploded on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Jaramana, a suburb of Damascus, killing two people, including a child, and wounding at least one, Syrian state media and the Interior Ministry said. State TV reported two people wounded, while the ministry reported one. Al Jazeera identified the dead as a man an
world.content: A bomb planted in a car exploded on Saturday, Nov. 14, in Jaramana, a suburb of Damascus, killing two people, including a child, and wounding at least one, Syrian state media and the Interior Ministry said. State TV reported two people wounded, while the ministry reported one. Al Jazeera identified the dead as a man and his daughter and reported that a third person, said to be the man's wife, was seriously injured. Security forces sealed off the scene and opened an investigation. Jaramana has a large Druze community and has seen tensions between some Druze residents and Sunni Muslims who support President Ahmed al-Sharaa’s government. Syria has experienced repeated attacks since Bashar Assad was ousted in December 2024; authorities have blamed some earlier attacks on Islamic State-linked cells.

world.title: Congo Ebola outbreak tops 11,000 cases as containment falters
world.summary: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control six months after authorities declared it on May 15, with more than 11,000 cases and over 5,400 deaths, according to government figures. The virus has reached eight provinces, and experts say current containment efforts are unlikely to bri
world.content: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains out of control six months after authorities declared it on May 15, with more than 11,000 cases and over 5,400 deaths, according to government figures. The virus has reached eight provinces, and experts say current containment efforts are unlikely to bring it under control within the next year. Contact tracing and isolation remain inadequate as fighting and attacks on health workers and facilities impede the response in eastern Congo. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has said 80% of new cases are detected outside the surveillance system, while aid groups have questioned how response funds reach patients and frontline staff. Health workers have repeatedly stopped work over months of unpaid wages, and children have accounted for a disproportionate share of deaths. Clinical trials of vaccines and treatments are underway in Bunia.

world.title: France protests draw 106,000 as unions plan fresh strike Tuesday
world.summary: About 106,000 people demonstrated across France on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to the Interior Ministry, as protests over living costs, public services and police accountability continued for a fifth weekend. Student unions put turnout at 200,000. The ministry counted 24,000 demonstrators in Paris and said 219 people
world.content: About 106,000 people demonstrated across France on Saturday, Nov. 14, according to the Interior Ministry, as protests over living costs, public services and police accountability continued for a fifth weekend. Student unions put turnout at 200,000. The ministry counted 24,000 demonstrators in Paris and said 219 people were detained nationwide. Police used tear gas in several cities, while authorities described most marches as peaceful. The demonstrations bring together students, unions and Yellow Vest activists. The protests began with student actions over teacher shortages and school conditions, then widened to include anger over prices, wages and alleged police violence. Protesters also opposed a bill that would give officers greater legal protection when they fire their weapons. Supporters say it would prevent officers from being automatically presumed to have used excessive force, while opponents say it could impede accountability. Unions have called a strike for Tuesday, Nov. 17, rejecting the government’s proposed 0.6% minimum-wage increase. The police bill is due to go before the Senate next week. Reports cited polls showing the far right leading ahead of France’s 2027 presidential election.
world.image_alt: France protests draw 106,000 as unions plan fresh strike Tuesday

world.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook photo access
world.summary: Italy’s data-protection authority fined Meta Platforms Ireland €805 million on Nov. 14, finding that Facebook’s Android app accessed Italian users’ photos, videos and related metadata without specific consent or adequate notice. The case concerns a feature, available since 2023, that suggests gallery images for posts;
world.content: Italy’s data-protection authority fined Meta Platforms Ireland €805 million on Nov. 14, finding that Facebook’s Android app accessed Italian users’ photos, videos and related metadata without specific consent or adequate notice. The case concerns a feature, available since 2023, that suggests gallery images for posts; the authority estimated that it affected about 20 million Android users. The regulator said Facebook sought gallery access through a general permission and a notice that did not clearly explain the suggestions feature. It said the feature was enabled by default and the alleged infringement continued for some users. Meta said it would appeal, calling the penalty disproportionate and arguing that users must grant device permission to use the feature. Italy ordered Meta to keep the feature off by default and obtain separate, clear consent within 60 days, including from users who had previously granted general access. The authority also requires Meta to report on its initial steps within 30 days and on completed measures within 90 days.
world.image_alt: Italy fines Meta €805 million over Facebook photo access

world.title: Russia confirms Trump-Xi-Putin meeting, but China has yet to commit
world.summary: Russia confirmed Saturday that President Vladimir Putin will meet U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The White House announced the three leaders’ first joint meeting on Friday, but China has not publicly
world.content: Russia confirmed Saturday that President Vladimir Putin will meet U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The White House announced the three leaders’ first joint meeting on Friday, but China has not publicly confirmed it. The White House says Trump plans to discuss nuclear arms reductions and the war in Iran, while Ukraine is not expected to be on the agenda. A senior U.S. official said Washington is handling Ukraine through a separate channel with Kyiv and Moscow and does not expect an agreement from the three-way meeting. The nuclear discussion follows the February expiration of the last U.S.-Russia arms-control treaty. U.S. officials describe the summit as an opening conversation, not a deal-making session. China has shown little interest in a nuclear pact, and its arsenal remains far smaller than those of Russia and the United States.
world.image_alt: Russia confirms Trump-Xi-Putin meeting, but China has yet to commit

world.title: ASEAN leaders open Manila summit with conflicts, energy and trade on agenda
world.summary: Southeast Asian leaders opened the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Sunday, Nov. 15, for three days of talks on trade, security and energy, including conflicts in the Middle East, Ukraine, Myanmar and the South China Sea. Draft summit statements call for respect for international law a
world.content: Southeast Asian leaders opened the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Sunday, Nov. 15, for three days of talks on trade, security and energy, including conflicts in the Middle East, Ukraine, Myanmar and the South China Sea. Draft summit statements call for respect for international law and the peaceful resolution of disputes. Leaders are also expected to address the economic effects of global conflicts. President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive Tuesday, after the main ASEAN meetings, for talks that include a meeting bringing together the United States, India, Japan and Australia. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. is due to meet him Wednesday. The Philippines is due to hand the bloc’s rotating chairmanship to Singapore.

world.title: Filipino singer Carmelle wins inaugural Eurovision Asia contest with 211 points
world.summary: Filipino singer Carmelle Collado won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia on Nov. 14 in Bangkok, earning 211 points with “Sobra-Sobra” and beating 10 other acts. Thailand finished second with 170 points and Vietnam third with 164. National juries and viewers around the world contributed to the result. The 19-year-old
world.content: Filipino singer Carmelle Collado won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia on Nov. 14 in Bangkok, earning 211 points with “Sobra-Sobra” and beating 10 other acts. Thailand finished second with 170 points and Vietnam third with 164. National juries and viewers around the world contributed to the result. The 19-year-old said the pop-and-rap song was a tribute to Filipino women and female empowerment. Eleven countries competed in the debut, which organisers presented as a new Asian edition of the 70-year-old European contest. Eurovision Asia executive producer Assaf Blecher said 16 or 17 territories had expressed interest in competing in 2027, including China, Hong Kong and Taiwan. Organisers will choose future hosts through a bidding process rather than automatically awarding hosting rights to the winning country. Carmelle is also due to perform at the European contest in Burgas in 2027.

world.title: Israeli strike kills Hamas Rafah brigade commander in southern Gaza
world.summary: Israel killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas’s Rafah brigade, in an airstrike in Khan Younis on Saturday, Nov. 14. Hamas confirmed his death the following day. Israel’s military and Shin Bet said they had targeted a senior figure in Hamas’s armed wing, while Hamas confirmed Abu Younis’s role as commander and said
world.content: Israel killed Samir Abu Younis, commander of Hamas’s Rafah brigade, in an airstrike in Khan Younis on Saturday, Nov. 14. Hamas confirmed his death the following day. Israel’s military and Shin Bet said they had targeted a senior figure in Hamas’s armed wing, while Hamas confirmed Abu Younis’s role as commander and said he helped plan and oversee the Oct. 7, 2023, attack on Israel. Medics said the strike hit Abu Younis on a street in the al-Mawasi area and wounded two other people. Israel said it used precision munitions and aerial surveillance to limit civilian harm; Al Jazeera reported that the strike hit a tent sheltering displaced people. The attack took place during a ceasefire that began in October 2025 and halted major fighting but has not ended Israeli strikes or secured Hamas’s disarmament. Gaza’s Health Ministry said that, as of Saturday, Israeli attacks had killed 1,643 Palestinians and wounded 5,964 since the truce began. The ministry also reports more than 74,000 Palestinians killed since the war began in October 2023.
world.image_alt: Israeli strike kills Hamas Rafah brigade commander in southern Gaza

business.title: Former adviser accuses Commerce chief of lax Nvidia chip controls
business.summary: Former National Security Council China director Liza Tobin accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to enforce U.S. export controls involving Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed, which is under scrutiny over suspected Chinese access to advanced Nvidia chips. The dispute centers on the company’s al
business.content: Former National Security Council China director Liza Tobin accused Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick of failing to enforce U.S. export controls involving Singapore-based data-center company Megaspeed, which is under scrutiny over suspected Chinese access to advanced Nvidia chips. The dispute centers on the company’s alleged ties to Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence suspects of working for Chinese intelligence. China denies the spying allegation. Tobin also said a firm run by Lutnick’s sons has a financial interest in the Asian data-center business, prompting questions about a possible conflict of interest. The Commerce Department said Lutnick had complied with his ethics agreement and divested his interests in Cantor Fitzgerald, Newmark and BGC. House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast has sought a Dec. 2 hearing on chip smuggling and reported interference in export-control decisions. Lawmakers have also demanded records related to the matter.
business.image_alt: Former adviser accuses Commerce chief of lax Nvidia chip controls

business.title: Nvidia CEO exit rattles AI shares as investors debate buying the dip
business.summary: Nvidia’s longtime chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned as president, CEO and board member on Nov. 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress took over on an interim basis while the board considers internal and outside candidates. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% at the open that day, and the company lost about $2 tri
business.content: Nvidia’s longtime chief executive, Jensen Huang, resigned as president, CEO and board member on Nov. 12. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress took over on an interim basis while the board considers internal and outside candidates. Nvidia shares fell more than 13% at the open that day, and the company lost about $2 trillion in market value during the week. Investors are weighing the company’s growth prospects against the absence of a named successor and concerns about how much of the artificial-intelligence trade depends on Nvidia. Funds holding double-leveraged Nvidia positions attracted about $900 million in a week, while retail investors bought a net $111 million of Nvidia shares in the first 30 minutes of Thursday trading. Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Nov. 17; three House committee chairs have also asked Huang to attend a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18.
business.image_alt: Nvidia CEO exit rattles AI shares as investors debate buying the dip

business.title: Anthropic seeks $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion valuation in IPO
business.summary: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering is entering its final week as banks pitch the Claude maker to investors with a more subdued campaign than the one for SpaceX’s June listing. Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion as investors become more selective about high valuations and s
business.content: Anthropic’s planned initial public offering is entering its final week as banks pitch the Claude maker to investors with a more subdued campaign than the one for SpaceX’s June listing. Anthropic is seeking a valuation of about $1.3 trillion to $1.4 trillion as investors become more selective about high valuations and spending plans. The company expects to set its IPO price on Nov. 18 and begin trading on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. Separately, Volatility Shares filed for a proposed exchange-traded fund designed to deliver twice Anthropic’s daily share-price movement.

business.title: Boston Fed chief backs gradual rate hikes as inflation pressures broaden
business.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said Nov. 14 she favors steady, modest interest-rate increases, arguing that inflation remains high and price pressures are spreading while the labor market is stable and could strengthen. She also warned that economic shocks and higher longer-term borrowing rates
business.content: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said Nov. 14 she favors steady, modest interest-rate increases, arguing that inflation remains high and price pressures are spreading while the labor market is stable and could strengthen. She also warned that economic shocks and higher longer-term borrowing rates could restrain demand, making faster increases risky. The Fed last raised its benchmark rate in September, leaving its target range at 3.75% to 4%; markets widely expect a quarter-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting and another in January. Collins said recent price data and a stronger labor market could mean a somewhat higher path for the policy rate over the next year than she expected a few months ago. She stressed that gradual increases do not dictate a fixed schedule.
business.image_alt: Boston Fed chief backs gradual rate hikes as inflation pressures broaden

business.title: Italy’s €805 million Meta fine equals about 0.4% of annual revenue
business.summary: Italy’s €805 million fine against Meta is equivalent to about 0.4% of the company’s 2025 revenue of $201 billion. Meta reported $60.5 billion in net profit that year. Italy’s data-protection authority said the penalty reflected the number of affected users, the duration of the practice and Meta’s lack of cooperation du
business.content: Italy’s €805 million fine against Meta is equivalent to about 0.4% of the company’s 2025 revenue of $201 billion. Meta reported $60.5 billion in net profit that year. Italy’s data-protection authority said the penalty reflected the number of affected users, the duration of the practice and Meta’s lack of cooperation during its investigation. The regulator fined Meta Platforms Ireland, Facebook’s Irish subsidiary, over the app’s access to Android users’ photo galleries. Meta said it would appeal, disputing both the regulator’s assessment and the size of the penalty. Its subsidiary also challenged Italy’s jurisdiction. Meta also faces a separate $25 billion New Mexico court order, The Guardian reported.
business.image_alt: Italy’s €805 million Meta fine equals about 0.4% of annual revenue

business.title: Bank of England economist signals rate rises through 2027
business.summary: Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said the central bank will probably need to raise interest rates again in December and continue raising them in 2027 to curb inflation. The Bank raised its rate from 3.75% to 4% in November, its first increase since August 2023. UK inflation is 3.5%, and the Bank expects it to r
business.content: Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said the central bank will probably need to raise interest rates again in December and continue raising them in 2027 to curb inflation. The Bank raised its rate from 3.75% to 4% in November, its first increase since August 2023. UK inflation is 3.5%, and the Bank expects it to reach about 5% next year as higher energy costs risk feeding into wages and other prices. Pill said market expectations that rates could approach 5% in 2027 were “not outrageous,” though he said the need for increases beyond December depends on incoming pay and pricing data. The Bank’s next rate decision is scheduled for December 17, and officials remain divided over how soon further action is needed.
business.image_alt: Bank of England economist signals rate rises through 2027

business.title: US-China business summit faces trade, AI and export-control disputes
business.summary: U.S. executives are expected to attend a business summit in Shenzhen alongside this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, with trade friction, competition over artificial intelligence and technology export controls shaping U.S.-China business ties. APEC’s 21 member economies account for more than 60%
business.content: U.S. executives are expected to attend a business summit in Shenzhen alongside this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting, with trade friction, competition over artificial intelligence and technology export controls shaping U.S.-China business ties. APEC’s 21 member economies account for more than 60% of global gross domestic product, and the summit agenda includes trade, digital commerce and AI. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to meet on the sidelines of APEC, while U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to join a separate U.S.-China dialogue on AI. U.S. officials say they do not plan to discuss chip export controls with China, describing them as national security decisions the administration makes.
business.image_alt: US-China business summit faces trade, AI and export-control disputes

business.title: US inflation prompts forecasts of three straight Fed rate hikes
business.summary: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than economists expected, prompting several analysts to forecast a Federal Reserve rate increase in December and two more in January and March. The Fed aims to return inflation to its 2% target; higher rates would raise borrowing costs for consumers. Bank of America econo
business.content: U.S. consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, more than economists expected, prompting several analysts to forecast a Federal Reserve rate increase in December and two more in January and March. The Fed aims to return inflation to its 2% target; higher rates would raise borrowing costs for consumers. Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave and TD Securities now expect quarter-point increases at the next three Fed meetings; TD had previously forecast two hikes. Traders put the odds of a quarter-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting near 90%, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller has argued policymakers should consider a half-point increase. The Fed’s next meeting is scheduled for Dec. 8-9.
business.image_alt: US inflation prompts forecasts of three straight Fed rate hikes

science.title: Apollo 12 lightning strikes prompted NASA to tighten launch weather rules
science.summary: Lightning struck NASA’s Apollo 12 Saturn V rocket twice within seconds of its Nov. 14, 1969, launch, disrupting spacecraft telemetry and endangering the mission. Mission Control engineer John Aaron recognized the readings from an earlier test and recommended switching the Signal Conditioning Equipment to its auxiliary
science.content: Lightning struck NASA’s Apollo 12 Saturn V rocket twice within seconds of its Nov. 14, 1969, launch, disrupting spacecraft telemetry and endangering the mission. Mission Control engineer John Aaron recognized the readings from an earlier test and recommended switching the Signal Conditioning Equipment to its auxiliary setting, which restored the data. Investigators concluded the rocket and its conductive exhaust plume had triggered a discharge in an electrically charged part of the atmosphere, even though no active thunderstorm lay along the immediate flight path. NASA expanded launch weather restrictions to account for atmospheric electrical conditions, not only visible lightning and thunderstorms.
science.image_alt: Apollo 12 lightning strikes prompted NASA to tighten launch weather rules

science.title: UN climate chief urges COP31 deal as fossil fuel divisions persist
science.summary: United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, to move quickly on a climate agreement as talks entered their second and final week, warning against “tactical delays.” Countries remain divided over stronger commitments to move away from oil, gas and coal, and over Tur
science.content: United Nations climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkey, to move quickly on a climate agreement as talks entered their second and final week, warning against “tactical delays.” Countries remain divided over stronger commitments to move away from oil, gas and coal, and over Turkey’s proposal to increase electricity’s share of global energy use without requiring that power to come from renewables. The talks also cover climate finance for developing countries, methane emissions and a just transition for workers. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for immediate emissions cuts and more funding, saying even tripling adaptation finance would cover less than 30% of the amount needed. The United States is absent for the second consecutive year under President Donald Trump. Australia’s negotiator Chris Bowen said a first draft of the agreement was expected early next week; the summit is scheduled to end next Friday.
science.image_alt: UN climate chief urges COP31 deal as fossil fuel divisions persist

science.title: California governor backs global fossil-fuel phaseout at COP31
science.summary: California Gov. Gavin Newsom endorsed a global transition away from oil, gas and coal at the COP31 United Nations climate summit in Turkey, calling for rapid adoption of clean energy. After the summit, he signed a climate partnership with Poland’s Ministry of Climate and Environment in Warsaw, covering clean energy, po
science.content: California Gov. Gavin Newsom endorsed a global transition away from oil, gas and coal at the COP31 United Nations climate summit in Turkey, calling for rapid adoption of clean energy. After the summit, he signed a climate partnership with Poland’s Ministry of Climate and Environment in Warsaw, covering clean energy, pollution cuts and climate resilience. Eighteen Democratic lawmakers also attended COP31 on Nov. 14, saying they aimed to reaffirm U.S. climate action while President Donald Trump’s administration boycotted the talks. The lawmakers said states and local governments continued to advance climate policies. Democrats also planned congressional investigations and clean-energy legislation after their midterm election gains.
science.image_alt: California governor backs global fossil-fuel phaseout at COP31

science.title: NASA
science.summary: NASA’s Voyager 1 is expected to become the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, when its radio signals will take 24 hours to reach the planet from more than 26 billion kilometers away. Launched in 1977, the probe still sends science and engineering data from interstellar s
science.content: NASA’s Voyager 1 is expected to become the first human-made object to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth on Nov. 18, when its radio signals will take 24 hours to reach the planet from more than 26 billion kilometers away. Launched in 1977, the probe still sends science and engineering data from interstellar space. Controllers completed a power-saving measure in September, then briefly lost contact with Voyager 1 in October. NASA is still investigating the communication disruption. The twin Voyagers measure magnetic fields, surrounding pressure, dust and galactic cosmic rays, with data arriving almost daily. NASA estimates Voyager 1 will need another 18,000 years to travel a light-year and more than twice as long to approach another star. To mark the milestone, NASA has invited people to flash “VGR” in Morse code after sunset on Nov. 17.

science.title: Ancient rock chemistry suggests plate tectonics began 2.5 billion years ago
science.summary: A chemical signal in ancient rocks disappears from the geological record about 2.5 billion years ago, a shift researchers say may mark the start of modern plate tectonics. The findings suggest Earth’s early continental crust formed through repeated remelting of ancient material before new crust began forming from a mix
science.content: A chemical signal in ancient rocks disappears from the geological record about 2.5 billion years ago, a shift researchers say may mark the start of modern plate tectonics. The findings suggest Earth’s early continental crust formed through repeated remelting of ancient material before new crust began forming from a mixture of old and fresh sources, a process the researchers compare with activity at present-day plate boundaries. The study examined more than 1,200 rocks from ancient landmasses in Australia, Africa, North America and Europe, spanning nearly four billion years. The researchers said the chemical signal’s disappearance coincided with other changes in rock chemistry and crustal composition, but they do not know what triggered the tectonic shift.
science.image_alt: Ancient rock chemistry suggests plate tectonics began 2.5 billion years ago

science.title: SpaceX tests Starship heat shield during first orbital-return catch
science.summary: SpaceX’s Starship Ship 42 returned from orbit on Saturday, Nov. 14, and launch-tower arms caught it at Starbase, Texas, in the first capture of an orbital spacecraft’s upper stage at its launch site. The test also gathered heat-shield data: cameras on three of the 26 Starlink V3 satellites photographed the spacecraft,
science.content: SpaceX’s Starship Ship 42 returned from orbit on Saturday, Nov. 14, and launch-tower arms caught it at Starbase, Texas, in the first capture of an orbital spacecraft’s upper stage at its launch site. The test also gathered heat-shield data: cameras on three of the 26 Starlink V3 satellites photographed the spacecraft, and SpaceX said the images showed the shield was in good condition for reentry. After about 14 orbits, Starship fired an engine to leave orbit, endured atmospheric heating and used its flaps to steer during descent before firing engines to turn upright for the catch. The flight did not establish whether the heat-shield tiles could be reused without significant inspection or repair. Engineers can now examine the recovered vehicle, but SpaceX has yet to demonstrate repeatable recoveries and rapid turnaround. For lunar missions, SpaceX also needs to dock Starships in orbit and transfer liquid methane and liquid oxygen between them. The New York Times reported that SpaceX could attempt that test next year.
science.image_alt: SpaceX tests Starship heat shield during first orbital-return catch

sports.title: Japan edge Brazil 3-2 as Sakamoto strikes in stoppage time
sports.summary: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 at Singapore’s National Stadium on November 14 after substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored his first international goal in the first minute of stoppage time. Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura had put Japan two goals ahead inside 19 minutes, but Vinícius Júnior scored twice, in the 33rd and 75th minu
sports.content: Japan beat Brazil 3-2 at Singapore’s National Stadium on November 14 after substitute Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scored his first international goal in the first minute of stoppage time. Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura had put Japan two goals ahead inside 19 minutes, but Vinícius Júnior scored twice, in the 33rd and 75th minutes, to bring Brazil level. Brazil appealed for a foul on midfielder João Gomes in the build-up to Sakamoto’s winner, but a video review upheld the goal. Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti and Barcelona captain Raphinha, who had been substituted in the 71st minute, were sent off for protesting. The friendly followed Japan’s defeat to Brazil at the 2026 World Cup. Japan next faces Paraguay and Brazil plays Singapore on November 17, both in the Mizuho Blue Challenge series in Singapore. Raphinha is suspended for Brazil’s match, while Ancelotti is also set to be absent from the touchline after his dismissal.
sports.image_alt: Japan edge Brazil 3-2 as Sakamoto strikes in stoppage time

sports.title: England post record 355 to set Australia 356-run Adelaide chase
sports.summary: England scored 355 for six in Adelaide on Sunday, their highest one-day international total in Australia, setting Australia 356 to win the second match of the three-game series. Australia led the series 1-0 after winning the Perth opener, leaving England needing to defend the target to level the series. Tom Banton made
sports.content: England scored 355 for six in Adelaide on Sunday, their highest one-day international total in Australia, setting Australia 356 to win the second match of the three-game series. Australia led the series 1-0 after winning the Perth opener, leaving England needing to defend the target to level the series. Tom Banton made 121 from 99 balls and Joe Root scored 62, before Jordan Cox’s 67 and Will Jacks’ unbeaten 54 lifted England’s total in the closing overs. The total was also the highest Australia have conceded in an ODI at Adelaide Oval. Australia’s chase was due to follow, with the deciding third ODI scheduled for Hobart on Wednesday, November 18.
sports.image_alt: England post record 355 to set Australia 356-run Adelaide chase

sports.title: Luke Littler opens Grand Slam defence with 5-2 win
sports.summary: World champion Luke Littler began his Grand Slam of Darts title defence in Wolverhampton on November 14 with a 5-2 win over Beau Greaves, extending his unbeaten run in the tournament to 15 matches. The 19-year-old world number one is seeking a third consecutive title, a feat previously achieved only by Phil Taylor and
sports.content: World champion Luke Littler began his Grand Slam of Darts title defence in Wolverhampton on November 14 with a 5-2 win over Beau Greaves, extending his unbeaten run in the tournament to 15 matches. The 19-year-old world number one is seeking a third consecutive title, a feat previously achieved only by Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen. Littler said his previous three or four majors had not gone well; he lost in the European Championship quarter-finals last month. The expanded event features 48 players in 16 groups of three, with 48 group-stage matches scheduled across the opening three days.
sports.image_alt: Luke Littler opens Grand Slam defence with 5-2 win

sports.title: Indiana beats USC 27-13, improves to 9-1
sports.summary: Indiana beat No. 18 Southern California 27-13 in Bloomington on Nov. 14, improving to 9-1 overall and 6-1 in the Big Ten. Seventh-year quarterback Grant Wilson, starting in place of Josh Hoover, threw for 305 yards and two touchdowns. His 42-yard scoring pass to Charlie Becker with 3:30 left helped seal the win. The re
sports.content: Indiana beat No. 18 Southern California 27-13 in Bloomington on Nov. 14, improving to 9-1 overall and 6-1 in the Big Ten. Seventh-year quarterback Grant Wilson, starting in place of Josh Hoover, threw for 305 yards and two touchdowns. His 42-yard scoring pass to Charlie Becker with 3:30 left helped seal the win. The reigning national champions’ playoff chances stood at 98% in an Athletic projection. A Big Ten title-game matchup with undefeated UCLA was the likeliest outcome, while USC fell to 7-3. Indiana visits Washington on Nov. 21 before hosting Purdue; USC hosts Maryland on Nov. 21.

sports.title: Meetmebythesea wins Paddy Power Gold Cup for owner McManus
sports.summary: Six-year-old Meetmebythesea won the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham on Saturday, giving owner JP McManus his first victory in the race. The 2-1 favourite, ridden by Harry Cobden and trained by Ben Pauling, beat Blueking D’Oroux by two and a half lengths. The win was Cobden’s first major success since becoming McManu
sports.content: Six-year-old Meetmebythesea won the Paddy Power Gold Cup at Cheltenham on Saturday, giving owner JP McManus his first victory in the race. The 2-1 favourite, ridden by Harry Cobden and trained by Ben Pauling, beat Blueking D’Oroux by two and a half lengths. The win was Cobden’s first major success since becoming McManus’s retained jockey in May and Meetmebythesea’s second Cheltenham victory, following a novice win at the March Festival. Pauling named the King George VI Chase at Kempton on Boxing Day as a possible next target but said the horse may need to improve further to win at the highest level.

sports.content: India were bowled out for 209 in the fifth ODI at Bay Oval on November 15, leaving New Zealand 210 to win and level the series. The hosts reached 87 for four, needing another 123 runs. Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh each took two wickets after New Zealand’s openers began steadily. India’s top order collapsed again: Rohit Sharma made seven, Virat Kohli five and Ruturaj Gaikwad 18, leaving the visitors 34 for three. Axar Patel and Ishan Kishan top-scored with 46 each, while Arshdeep and Siraj added 26 runs for the final wicket. India entered the decider 2-1 ahead after New Zealand won the fourth ODI by 244 runs and the third match was abandoned. The result will determine whether India win the series or the teams finish level. New Zealand have not lost a home bilateral ODI series since 2019.

sports.content: English golfer Tyrrell Hatton will take a one-shot lead into Sunday’s final round of the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai after shooting a four-under 68 on Saturday. Frenchman Victor Perez is second at eight under, while Northern Ireland’s Rory McIlroy and Spain’s Eugenio Chacarra are among four players tied for fourth at five under, four shots behind Hatton. The season finale also decides the Race to Dubai, the DP World Tour’s season-long points title. Chacarra leads McIlroy by about 534 points; a tournament win would guarantee McIlroy an eighth season title, matching the record held by Scotland’s Colin Montgomerie. The winner earns 2,000 points, and McIlroy must make up the gap by finishing ahead of Chacarra. Hatton, who has never won this championship, will play the final round alongside Perez. McIlroy tees off with England’s Dan Bradbury, while Chacarra is paired with Italy’s Francesco Laporta. Hatton’s Saturday round included an eagle, four birdies and two bogeys. He saved par at the 18th after finding water off the tee and a greenside bunker with his approach.

Sabalenka said the remark was aimed at a small group of spectators who cheered her mistakes, not at Svitolina, and that she should have handled her f
sports.content: Aryna Sabalenka apologized after a viral video showed her swearing and gesturing during her three-set loss to Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells on Friday. Sabalenka said the remark was aimed at a small group of spectators who cheered her mistakes, not at Svitolina, and that she should have handled her frustration differently. The clip prompted interpretations that Sabalenka’s words targeted Svitolina or Ukrainians. Russia’s war in Ukraine has strained relations between Ukrainian and Belarusian players. Svitolina said she hoped matches between them would be respected and that she has faced hostile online comments about the war. Svitolina then beat Linda Noskova to reach the final, where she is scheduled to face 19-year-old Russian player Mirra Andreeva on Sunday. Svitolina is seeking her second title at the $10 million season-ending tournament; Andreeva beat her in their earlier meeting this week.
